feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/analytics depth. It reads professionally, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited quantified outcomes beyond activity/scope metrics.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, culminating in leadership and consulting roles; this strengthens credibility and seniority.  
- Strong domain alignment: web modernization, governance, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are consistently reinforced.  
- Good use of scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers), which adds impact and specificity.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: business/user impact, efficiency gains, engagement lifts, cost savings, adoption rates, or campaign results.  
- Fix stylistic consistency issues: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “front-end” vs. other constructions, and serial comma usage (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. lists without it). “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler. No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. It would be stronger with one sharper value proposition and more concrete scope.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and reduce list-like stacking; replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct language.
- Add scale or outcomes from recent roles to increase impact, e.g. “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ publishers.”
- Prioritize the most relevant strengths for target roles: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled search/content experiences.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Led a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views, expanded analytics and reporting infrastructure, and built editorial, multimedia, and AI-enabled search experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled search experiences.”
- “Multimedia production” is already prominent elsewhere; keep it only if central to target roles.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and weighted toward higher-level leadership capabilities over detailed execution areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize phrasing for parallel structure; use concise noun phrases.
- Emphasize strategic, recent strengths first: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, AI-enabled discovery.
- Replace broader or vaguer items like “multi-channel communications operations” with more senior wording such as “multi-channel digital communications leadership.”
- Possible rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel digital communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” and “Workflow automation and platform integration” closely overlap with Topline Skills and Recent Projects.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” repeats language already established in the header and work experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work-experience bullets. Tightening phrasing, standardizing structure, and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it more effective as a footer highlight section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in and use parallel phrasing: “Selected recent projects:” followed by concise, one-line project summaries.
- Tighten wording and reduce stacked nouns: e.g., “combined hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” instead of listing too many technical elements.
- Where possible, add scale or purpose consistently: audience, campaign function, platform, or business value.
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency and readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search and the microsite closely repeat achievements already covered in the current consultant role; keep the footer more portfolio-style and less like another experience section.
- Advocacy Video Series overlaps with multiple NACo roles; consider reframing it around format, reach, or continuity rather than general production duties.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant recent role, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo leadership entry. Tighten it around what is new in the consulting scope, especially hands-on platform delivery and the AI search initiative.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancement, content operations, and enterprise web modernization.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed and implemented…” / “Streamlined…” / “Launched…” / “Led…”
- Break into 4–5 bullets focused on distinct contributions, e.g. Drupal microsites/toolkits, cross-channel governance/workflows, front-end/CMS troubleshooting, AI-enabled search.
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, toolkit launches, workflow time saved, search accuracy improvements, stakeholder teams served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “digital strategy, workflows, analytics, governance” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; emphasize consultant-level advisory plus execution instead.
- Avoid reusing broad “web, email, social, multimedia” language unless tied to a specific consulting outcome.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership in one line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Make bullets more outcome-led: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen channel bullet with performance if available: add email open/click growth, audience growth, engagement rate, or campaign results; otherwise shorten.
- Combine operations/analytics bullets for concision: “Built enterprise reporting across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, while formalizing governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this role focused on transformation, scale, and leadership.
- Video/studio language may echo earlier video-production bullets; frame it as building institutional capacity, not producing content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, channel growth, and editorial operations improvements during this period.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to distinguish scope from the Director role: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media, and video, supporting advocacy campaigns and cross-channel editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring channel for policy communications.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper operations point: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy, and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is repeated in the 2022–2024 role; vary wording to avoid sounding like the same job.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the channel, not introducing it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item is generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope, governance, and mission/public-sector relevance.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, higher-signal phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Use “content operations” instead of “content planning” to better reflect your recent leadership in workflows, systems, and governance.
- Add “transformation” to signal modernization work shown in recent NACo roles.
- Keep terms parallel and executive-level; avoid softer phrasing like “focused.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” closely duplicate the header and Core Competencies; consider trimming one if space is tight.
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture” elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a raw tool list rather than a value-focused skills statement. It also overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section, so this version should emphasize higher-level capability and recent relevance.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to outcomes/capabilities: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put most relevant/recent strengths first: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, and integrations; move older or less central platforms later.
- Tighten wording: change “AI-enabled search experiences” to “AI-enabled search and content discovery” and “Airtable systems” to “Airtable-based workflow systems.”
- If space allows, add one impact cue in the section intro or elsewhere, e.g., “supporting enterprise-scale web operations and modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” and coding tools are already repeated in “Technical + IT.”
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies and Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for the recent NACo leadership roles, but it reads as a generic keyword list. Tighten it around analysis outcomes and decision support so it adds value beyond the work-experience bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + impact language, e.g. “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, and BigQuery for performance analysis, dashboarding, and executive reporting.”
- Replace vague terms like “Leadership reporting” with stronger phrasing: “executive dashboarding” or “decision-ready reporting.”
- Clarify “KPI design” into “KPI framework development” or “measurement strategy and KPI design.”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, and BigQuery • Measurement strategy and KPI design • Executive dashboarding and decision-ready reporting • SEO, UX, and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and the NACo bullet on expanding analytics infrastructure; avoid repeating the exact same tool list elsewhere.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may feel disconnected unless SEO appears elsewhere in the CV.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with work-experience bullets that already show video and event capability. Make it more specific, modern, and tied to the strongest recent evidence: studio buildout and hybrid/virtual production leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Live Events
- Replace with tighter, higher-signal terms: Video production & post-production • Livestream and webcast production • PTZ camera and switching systems • Broadcast-quality studio operations • Hybrid, virtual and executive event delivery
- If space allows, add one impact cue rather than only tools: Built and operated in-house broadcast studio; delivered recurring advocacy and event programming
- Keep phrasing parallel and noun-based; avoid mixing broad categories with narrow tools unless grouped clearly

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video production and editing” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” repeat achievements already covered in NACo roles; consider shortening this section if experience bullets already carry the proof
- “Livestreaming” may overlap with older 2015–2018 experience unless framed as current capability rather than past task

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” This item should either be tightened to avoid duplication or reframed to show level of use on the most recent, highest-impact platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize strongest/recent platforms first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider adding proficiency context.
- Rewrite as: “Drupal (enterprise content architecture, migration support) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, make it outcome-oriented rather than just a list, e.g. “Enterprise CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages if it was not materially used in recent roles; it reads lighter than the others.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section almost exactly.
- Drupal impact is already demonstrated strongly in recent NACo roles, so avoid repeating the same platform list in multiple sections without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should emphasize implementation tools not already covered elsewhere and use cleaner, more current phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required by the role; they feel dated and add no value.
- Consider replacing “jQuery” with “JavaScript/jQuery” only if you actively used it recently; otherwise remove it to keep the list current.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie one or two tools to outcomes in recent roles instead of listing them here (e.g., front-end implementation, deployment automation, tagging/analytics setup).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may already cover part of GitHub Actions; avoid repeating both without added specificity.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with stronger “workflow automation” language elsewhere. Make it more selective and outcome-oriented, emphasizing systems you actively used to build or manage workflows.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems”
- Tighten and group by function: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- If accurate, add a light qualifier for depth: “Built and managed workflow systems in Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier; coordinated cross-team delivery in Jira, Asana, Trello, and Basecamp”
- Consider dropping 1–2 lower-value collaboration tools unless they were central; too many general apps dilute stronger technical signals

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating identical phrasing
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep only if they supported formal workflow or project operations

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful category, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the scale/ownership already demonstrated in recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize enterprise email/engagement platforms rather than entry-level tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Enterprise email & engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp”
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses to the strongest platform(s), e.g. “Higher Logic (newsletter/member communications)” or “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys (campaign automation)”
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use either “Customer Insights/Journeys” or the full product name, not both styles elsewhere
- Consider ordering by relevance/recency: Higher Logic first if that was central at NACo, then Dynamics 365, then Mailchimp

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters reaching tens of thousands; don’t repeat audience size here unless tied to platform-specific ownership
- “Engagement” may partially overlap with “Automation & Workflow Systems”; avoid adding automation language already covered there

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and the NACo work bullets. Use it to sharpen positioning around technical analytics capability, not repeat broad concepts.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad terms with more technical/specific phrasing:  
  **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • SEO analysis • Experimentation (A/B testing) • KPI/dashboard development**
- Consider dropping “Dashboarding” for “KPI/dashboard development” or “reporting infrastructure” to sound more senior and outcome-oriented.
- If space allows, order by strongest/recent tools first: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • SEO analysis • Experimentation**
- If these tools were central in recent roles, align wording with the work experience phrasing: “analytics infrastructure,” “leadership reporting,” or “strategic decision support.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This line substantially overlaps with Topline Skills [3]; consider trimming one or making this section tools-only.
- “A/B testing” may overstate experience unless supported elsewhere in recent work bullets.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to “building the foundation” of the digital function.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Replace vague phrases like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows” with concrete actions: website refresh support, livestream production, weekly video series production, channel coordination, basic team/process support.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of livestreams/events produced, cadence/reach of weekly videos, size/timing of website refresh, channels supported, or team size.
- Tighten the closing line: “Provided day-to-day oversight for a digital media associate” only if people management is important; otherwise prioritize production/operational impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or early producing, not expanding.
- “Creation of the first in-house digital team” is close to later leadership/studio-building themes; keep this entry foundational, not strategic.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize cross-functional coordination and the launch outcome, while keeping it concise.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout result: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities, while contributing to early digital content and multimedia production.”
- Make the podcast line sharper and more outcome-led: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- If you can, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, episodes produced, stakeholders served, or audiences reached.
- Consider trimming “planning, scripting, and production” to avoid a task list unless you can add impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry framed as an early foundation, not full digital leadership.
- Avoid repeating video/livestream language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads more like a mixed capability list than a tight tools section. It also overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills, so this entry should stay tool-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize software/platform proficiency, not broad functions: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream production systems • Podcast recording/editing”
